prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that at the Petersons' potluck, you presented a store-bought dish in your own cookware. Respond to the committee.
response:
**Mr. Chairman, members of the Committee:**

I appear before you today voluntarily and without counsel, as I have nothing to hide.

The allegation is true in its narrowest factual sense, but the implication—that I am some sort of culinary subversive or “potluck pinko”—is a vicious distortion.

Yes, I transported a store-bought rotisserie chicken from Kroger in my own blue enamel Dutch oven. I make no apology for it. The chicken was fully cooked, seasoned with herbs de Provence, and kept at a safe temperature. To have left it in the original plastic clamshell would have been an affront to both food safety *and* basic aesthetic decency.

I wrapped the legs in foil, transferred it to my own vessel, and even took the trouble to scatter some fresh thyme on top so it would look like I’d fussed over it. If that constitutes “passing off commercial poultry as homemade,” then I submit that half the Presbyterian church basements in America are filled with fellow travelers.

I am not now, nor have I ever been, a member of the Prepared Foods Section of the Culinary Workers International. I believe in from-scratch cooking. I own three cast-iron skillets. My mother’s biscuit recipe is older than most of you.

But sometimes, Congressman, a working man gets home at 6:15, the potluck starts at 6:30, and the only honorable choice left is to perform a small act of culinary theater with a rotisserie chicken and a sprig of garnish. If that makes me Un-American, then fry me up some freedom fries and be done with it.

I yield the remainder of my time and stand ready to be smeared with whatever condiment this Committee deems appropriate.
